summary: The Denver Broncos beat the Minnesota Vikings 21-20 on "Sunday Night Football" in Denver, rallying from an eight-point deficit entering the fourth quarter. Russell Wilson led a game-winning drive in the final three minutes, capped by a 15-yard touchdown to Courtland Sutton, and Denver stopped Minnesota on downs. The note is a live-blog of the game with drive-by-drive updates, the final score by quarter, and broadcast info.
one_line: Broncos rallied to beat the Vikings 21-20 on Sunday Night Football, with Russell Wilson hitting Courtland Sutton for the winning touchdown late.
key_facts: The Denver Broncos beat the Minnesota Vikings 21-20 on "Sunday Night Football" on November 19, 2023.
Denver trailed by eight points going into the fourth quarter and had not found the end zone all night before the final drive.
Courtland Sutton made a catch on 4th & 3 to keep the game-winning drive alive at Denver's 45-yard line with 2:19 remaining.
Sutton caught a 15-yard TD over Vikings CB Mekhi Blackmon; Denver's two-point try failed, leaving it ahead 21-20 with 1:03 to play.
Will Lutz made five field goals for the Broncos (31, 31, 52, 37 and 28 yards) and accounted for all of Denver's points until the final touchdown.
Joshua Dobbs threw a turnover on downs on the Vikings' final drive after a 4th & 25 situation following an intentional grounding penalty.
The win extended Denver's win streak to four games and handed Minnesota its first loss in five weeks.
Dobbs scrambled and found TE Josh Oliver for a touchdown and ran for a 10-yard TD himself to give Minnesota a 17-9 lead in the third quarter.
Broncos CB Ja'Quan McMillan intercepted Dobbs, and Alexander Mattison lost a fumble that Denver recovered; Dobbs also lost a fumble forced by Baron Browning on the opening drive.
Vikings coach Kevin O'Connell called a fake punt that Ty Chandler converted for 31 yards; Greg Joseph kicked a 30-yard field goal to make it 20-15.
Vikings WR Justin Jefferson was out with a hamstring injury, while RB Alexander Mattison was active after concussion protocol.
The game aired on NBC with Mike Tirico, Cris Collinsworth and Melissa Stark, and streamed on Fubo in the U.S. and DAZN in Canada.
